messages:
alex: Heads-up — we need to handle a few org-level shared API key exceptions for telemetry and legacy infra agents. Proposing we treat them as scoped-but-exempt for RBAC checks, with explicit audit-only flags. Thoughts?

sam: do you mean some keys would bypass project-level RBAC and use org-level allowlists?

alex: yeah. example: legacy deployer that lives in infra project but needs to call multiple customer projects for health checks. We don't want to give it a full org-admin role. Idea: short-lived org-scoped key with a narrow capability set + audit logging and CIDR restrictions.

maria: Concern: every bypass increases blast radius. Audit-only flags are fine but we need runtime enforcement for attribute checks (origin IP, service identity) not just role.

jordan: +1 to origin checks. Also prefer ephemeral tokens minted by a broker rather than long-lived org keys. Broker can encode claims (projects allowed, expiry, nonce) so downstream services can verify without central call.

sam: how would broker auth work with existing service accounts? We have service-auth and project bindings today. Would this add a new claim type?

alex: Broker flow: service authenticates with its service credential (existing project-scoped), requests an org-proxy token with allowed-targets list. Broker enforces policy (mfa, approval, owner oncall) and issues short TTL token signed by org key. Token includes allowed-targets and audit id.

maria: That seems reasonable. Two questions: 1) who can request such a token (roles)? 2) how to revoke quickly if compromise?

jordan: For 1) we should gate by a new role: org-proxy-requester, limited to specific service principals. For 2) use short TTL (5-15m) + a revocation list published to edge caches. If we need instant cut, rotate org signing key and push revocation ID — heavier but possible.

sam: implementational tradeoff: verifying signed tokens locally vs central introspect. Local verify scales better but forces token format stability and key distribution. Introspect simpler but adds latency and availability dependency.

alex: agree. For scale and SLOs we should prefer local verification with key rotation via signed JWKS. Introspect can be fallback for very sensitive flows.

maria: Also add telemetry: every broker issue must log requestor, allowed-targets, justification, and link to audit trail. Make it searchable in Console.

security-bot: Note: existing policy RFC 2023-09 requires audit events for cross-project calls. This thread proposal aligns but needs an explicit exception list and migration plan.

alex: Next steps I propose: 1) draft short RFC for org-proxy broker (scope, token format, TTL, roles), 2) prototype broker + local JWT verification library, 3) migration plan for legacy infra clients. I'll start the RFC and tag folks. Any objections?

sam: no objections. please include performance targets for verification (<1ms) and key rotation plan.

maria: add an attack model section (token theft, replay, compromised broker). Also include plan for monitoring anomalous allowed-targets requests.

jordan: I'll help with the broker prototype and key distribution.

alex: thanks — I'll open the RFC draft this afternoon and ping in #eng-security. :thumbsup:
